description: Integrate IoT backend with MCP server: create 7 new MCP tools (registerIoTDevice, deregisterIoTDevice, getDeviceStatus, listDevicesByZone, getDeviceTelemetry, anomalyReport, subscribeToZoneStream), 4 new MCP resources (tradeops://iot/devices, tradeops://iot/device/{deviceId}, tradeops://iot/telemetry/{zoneId}, tradeops://iot/anomalies), set RBAC tiers, add HTTP endpoints (POST /webhooks/telemetry, GET /sse/:zoneId) to transport layer. Depends on FEAT-001 (IoT backend). Independent of FEAT-003 (UI).
steps: Create src/tools/iot.ts with 7 tool handlers following pattern in src/tools/customs.ts. Each handler: async function(args, ctx: RequestContext, deps: ToolDeps, approvalToken?: string) returning { type: 'text', text: JSON.stringify(result) }[]. Tools: registerIoTDevice (requires approvalToken, calls registry.register, returns device), deregisterIoTDevice (requires approvalToken, calls registry.deregister, returns success), getDeviceStatus (calls registry.get, returns device or not found), listDevicesByZone (args: { zone }, calls registry.listByZone, returns devices array), getDeviceTelemetry (args: { deviceId, limit? }, queries ledger for iot.telemetry.received events filtered by deviceId, returns events), anomalyReport (queries ledger for iot.telemetry.received where payload.anomaly=true, returns anomaly events), subscribeToZoneStream (args: { zoneId }, returns SSE URL http://localhost:8787/sse/{zoneId} as text - MCP bridging, no real SSE connection from tool).

Modify src/tools/index.ts: import * as iot from './iot.js'. Add 7 tool definitions to tools array: { name: 'registerIoTDevice', description: 'Register IoT device in registry', schema: { device: z.object({ id: z.string(), type: z.enum(['RFID','barcode','GPS','sensor','camera']), zone: z.string(), location: z.string().optional(), firmware: z.string().optional(), lastSeen: z.string(), telemetrySchema: z.record(z.unknown()).optional() }), approvalToken: z.string() }, handler: iot.registerIoTDevice, requiresApprovalToken: true } and similar for other 6 tools. Update TOOL_COUNT from 27 to 34. In registerAllTools(), add setToolTier('registerIoTDevice', 'write'), setToolTier('deregisterIoTDevice', 'write'), setToolTier('getDeviceStatus', 'read'), setToolTier('listDevicesByZone', 'read'), setToolTier('getDeviceTelemetry', 'read'), setToolTier('anomalyReport', 'read'), setToolTier('subscribeToZoneStream', 'read').

Create src/resources/devices.ts with registerDeviceResources(server: McpServer, registry: DeviceRegistry). Register two resources: (1) 'iot-devices' at tradeops://iot/devices returning JSON with devices: registry.all(), count. (2) 'iot-device-by-id' at tradeops://iot/device/sample (template simulation) accepting deviceId from URI, calling registry.get(deviceId), returning device JSON or error. Follow pattern in src/resources/ledger.ts.

Create src/resources/telemetry.ts with registerTelemetryResources(server: McpServer, ledger: BondedLedger). Register two resources: (1) 'iot-telemetry-by-zone' at tradeops://iot/telemetry/sample (template simulation) accepting zoneId from URI, querying ledger.query({ zone: zoneId, eventType: 'iot.telemetry.received', limit: 20 }), returning events JSON. (2) 'iot-anomalies' at tradeops://iot/anomalies querying ledger for iot.telemetry.received events, filtering client-side where event.payload?.anomaly === true, returning anomaly events JSON.

Modify src/resources/index.ts: import { registerDeviceResources } from './devices.js'; import { registerTelemetryResources } from './telemetry.js'. In registerAllResources(), after existing registrations, add: await registerDeviceResources(server, deps.registry); await registerTelemetryResources(server, deps.ledger). Note: deps signature needs DeviceRegistry - coordinate with transport layer initialization.

Locate HTTP transport setup (likely in main entry point or src/transport/http.ts, check package.json bin field ./dist/index.js source). Add two Express routes BEFORE existing MCP route handlers to avoid conflicts: (1) app.post('/webhooks/telemetry', webhookHandler.handle.bind(webhookHandler)) where webhookHandler is instance of WebhookHandler from src/iot/webhookHandler.ts with deps: { registry, normalizer, ledger, broadcaster, secret: process.env.WEBHOOK_SECRET || 'dev-secret' }. (2) app.get('/sse/:zoneId', (req, res) => { const { zoneId } = req.params; broadcaster.subscribe(zoneId, res); req.on('close', () => broadcaster.unsubscribe(zoneId, res)); }) where broadcaster is instance of SSEBroadcaster from src/iot/sseBroadcaster.ts. Initialize DeviceRegistry, TelemetryNormalizer, ZoneGraphUpdater, SSEBroadcaster at server startup and pass to tools/resources as deps.

Update tests/tools.spec.ts: change 'registers exactly 27 tools' assertion to expect(TOOL_COUNT).toBe(34) and expect(TOOL_DEFINITIONS).toHaveLength(34). Add test block 'includes all IoT tools' checking for registerIoTDevice, deregisterIoTDevice, getDeviceStatus, listDevicesByZone, getDeviceTelemetry, anomalyReport, subscribeToZoneStream in TOOL_DEFINITIONS.map(t => t.name). Add test 'marks IoT write tools as requiring approval' checking registerIoTDevice and deregisterIoTDevice have requiresApprovalToken: true. Add test 'does not mark IoT read tools as requiring approval' checking getDeviceStatus, listDevicesByZone, getDeviceTelemetry, anomalyReport, subscribeToZoneStream have requiresApprovalToken !== true.
acceptance_criteria: src/tools/iot.ts exports 7 tool handler functions matching ToolHandler signature
src/tools/index.ts TOOL_COUNT = 34, tools array contains 7 IoT tool definitions, registerAllTools() sets RBAC tiers for all 7 IoT tools
tests/tools.spec.ts passes with 34 tools, includes all IoT tools, marks write tools as requiring approval
src/resources/devices.ts registers tradeops://iot/devices (list all) and tradeops://iot/device/{deviceId} (single device)
src/resources/telemetry.ts registers tradeops://iot/telemetry/{zoneId} (latest 20 events) and tradeops://iot/anomalies (all anomalies)
src/resources/index.ts calls registerDeviceResources and registerTelemetryResources in registerAllResources()
HTTP transport layer adds POST /webhooks/telemetry endpoint mounting WebhookHandler.handle middleware
HTTP transport layer adds GET /sse/:zoneId endpoint mounting SSEBroadcaster.subscribe with cleanup on connection close
Server initialization creates DeviceRegistry, TelemetryNormalizer, ZoneGraphUpdater, SSEBroadcaster instances and passes to tools/resources
Manual test: curl POST /webhooks/telemetry with valid payload → 200 OK, ledger event appended, SSE broadcast sent
Manual test: curl GET /sse/IOT → SSE stream with heartbeat comments every 30s
Manual test: MCP tool call registerIoTDevice → device registered, ledger event emitted
Manual test: MCP resource read tradeops://iot/devices → returns all devices JSON
verification: npm run typecheck (no TypeScript errors in src/tools/iot.ts, src/resources/devices.ts, src/resources/telemetry.ts, modified files)
npm test -- tools.spec.ts (tool count and IoT tool tests pass)
npm test (all Part A tests still pass, no regressions)
Manual: MCP_TRANSPORT=http node dist/index.js → server starts, logs show IoT components initialized

Manual: curl -X POST http://localhost:8787/mcp -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"registerIoTDevice","arguments":{"device":{"id":"rfid-001","type":"RFID","zone":"IOT","lastSeen":"2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"},"approvalToken":"test"}},"id":1}' → returns device JSON
Manual: curl -N http://localhost:8787/sse/IOT → SSE stream with heartbeats
